children: MediaTek shares surged 10% in Taipei trading on Tuesday, September 1, after Nvidia agreed to invest $3.5 billion in the Taiwanese chipmaker, marking the Jensen Huang-led company's largest ever direct investment outside the United States.
The stock hit its daily trading limit as investors welcomed the deal as a major vote of confidence in MediaTek's push into artificial intelligence chips.

The two companies announced the deepened partnership on Monday, August 31, in an official statement. Under the agreement, Nvidia will buy bonds convertible into MediaTek shares as part of a $3.9 billion US dollar-denominated convertible bond sale by MediaTek.

MediaTek was once known chiefly for competing with Qualcomm for mobile phone chip orders from manufacturers such as Xiaomi and Oppo. In recent years, the company has moved towards designing custom silicon, positioning itself against rivals such as Broadcom and building a reputation as a partner for major technology firms developing their own AI chips.

The deal came as Nvidia continued to deepen its involvement in AI infrastructure. Anthropic agreed to a $35 billion computing deal with Nvidia-backed cloud provider Lambda to expand its AI capacity, Bloomberg reported.
Jensen Huang, founder and chief executive of Nvidia, said AI was transforming every computing platform, from large AI factories to PCs and cars.
He described MediaTek as one of the world's great semiconductor companies, citing its expertise in system-on-chip design, connectivity and power efficiency.
Rick Tsai, MediaTek's vice chairman and chief executive, said the investment strengthened a collaboration spanning cloud AI infrastructure, local AI computing and automotive technology.
He added that combining Nvidia's computing and software strengths with MediaTek's silicon expertise would accelerate innovation for customers.

As part of the expanded partnership, MediaTek will adopt Nvidia's NVLink Fusion platform, giving hyperscalers and cloud providers a validated path to build custom processors that connect into Nvidia's rack-scale AI systems.
The companies will also continue collaborating on RTX Spark and DGX Spark PC chips, as well as automotive platforms for software-defined vehicles.

Tsai also said he expected MediaTek's AI chip business to accelerate following the Nvidia deal. The company had previously guided that its custom AI silicon business would reach $2 billion this year, with plans to capture 15% of an estimated $80 billion market segment by 2027.

MediaTek's market value has roughly tripled in recent months, aided by a partnership secured with Google earlier this year and speculation among analysts that SpaceX could become its next AI customer as per a Bloomberg report.
MSCI's Asia Pacific equities gauge rose 0.3% in early Asian trade, led by gains in Taiwanese shares.

title: MediaTek shares jump 10% after Nvidia's largest direct investment outside the US
